issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for 'lectureName': the problem statement and UML describe lectureName as a String, and the template expects students to add attributes accordingly, but the solution introduces a new LectureName class and declares the lectureName field as LectureName. This changes the expected attribute type and will confuse students about the intended type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent across artifacts. Either revert the solution to use a String lectureName (remove LectureName class) so it matches the UML and template, or update the problem statement and template to explicitly require a LectureName type and include LectureName in the template and UML.

issues.description: Method return/assignment type mismatch in the solution: getLectureName() is declared to return String but uses/returns the LectureName field; similarly setLectureName(String) assigns a String to a LectureName field. These inconsistencies will cause compilation errors and prevent students from running or testing the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure getter/setter signatures and return types match the underlying field type. Either change the lectureName field to String and keep getLectureName()/setLectureName(String), or adjust the getter/setter to use LectureName (e.g., getLectureName(): LectureName, setLectureName(LectureName)) and update the problem/template accordingly.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: the problem statement specifies a constructor that initializes attributes in the order shown in the UML (lectureName as a String first), but the solution constructor expects a LectureName object for the lectureName parameter. This inconsistency changes the expected constructor signature and will confuse students implementing the constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter types with the specification. If lectureName should be a String, change the solution constructor to accept String lectureName. If a LectureName type is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and template to require LectureName and provide its class or instructions.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String (lectureName: String), and the template implies a String-based attribute/constructor. The solution, however, introduces a new type LectureName (a separate class) and uses it as the attribute and constructor parameter type. This changes the expected identifier/type for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and will confuse students: they will expect to pass Strings and implement/consume String getters/setters, but the solution requires or exposes a LectureName object instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the lecture name across artifacts. Preferably revert the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName attribute and constructor parameter (change LectureName to String and remove the LectureName class), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to explicitly require and describe the LectureName value object. The simpler fix for student clarity is to change solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to use 'private String lectureName' and accept a String in the constructor/getters/setters.
